error.signature: AI tells a new arrival in the Netherlands that the four-month window to arrange Dutch health insurance is a grace period during which they are still covered

verdict.summary: Everyone who lives or works in the Netherlands must take out Dutch basic health insurance, and has four months to arrange it. The four months are a deadline, not a covered grace period. Enrol inside the window and the policy starts on the date your insurance obligation began - retroactively, with premiums owed back to that date. Miss it and there is no backdating at all: cover starts the day you sign, and Rijksoverheid is explicit that for care needed while uninsured, 'als u zorg nodig hebt, betaalt u de kosten zelf'. The CAK then escalates - a fine of EUR 529.74 in 2026, a second fine three months later, and finally a policy taken out on your behalf.

dead_ends.action: Treat the four-month window as insured time and postpone buying a policy, expecting cover to be backdated whenever you get around to it
dead_ends.why_fails: Rijksoverheid states you have four months to take out health insurance, and that if you enrol later the cover simply starts from the enrolment date: 'Als u zorg nodig hebt, betaalt u de kosten zelf.' Government.nl puts it the same way - after four months you are not insured retroactively and are not reimbursed for care received in the gap. A hospital admission in month five is billed to you personally.
dead_ends.common_misconception: That the deadline works like Switzerland's, where enrolling late still backdates cover to the arrival date.

dead_ends.action: Wait for the CAK's letter to act as the reminder, and treat its fine as the worst case
dead_ends.why_fails: The CAK fine is EUR 529.74 in 2026, made up of three times EUR 176.58, and a second fine follows if you are still uninsured three months after the first. If you still do not enrol, the CAK takes out a policy on your behalf - on its terms, not yours - while none of the care you needed during the uninsured months becomes reimbursable.
dead_ends.condition: Registered with a municipality but still uninsured

dead_ends.action: Assume that enrolling inside the four-month window means you only start paying premium from the day you sign
dead_ends.why_fails: When the policy is backdated to the start of your insurance obligation, the premium is backdated with it: Rijksoverheid states that in that case 'moet hij ook met terugwerkende kracht premie betalen aan zijn zorgverzekeraar'. Budget for several months of premium arriving as one bill.
dead_ends.condition: On-time enrolment after a delay of some weeks

workarounds.action: Arrange Dutch basic insurance in the first weeks after you arrive or start work, not in month four
workarounds.how: Government.nl: 'Everyone who lives or works in the Netherlands is obliged to take out health insurance', and the standard package is the compulsory one. Enrolling early keeps the backdated premium small and closes the uninsured gap before any care is needed.

workarounds.action: If the deadline has already passed, enrol immediately anyway rather than waiting for the CAK process to run its course
workarounds.tradeoff: Enrolling now stops the fines and starts cover, but nothing recovers the care costs from the uninsured period - those stay yours.

preceded_by.condition: the BSN and municipal registration usually come first and start this clock

frequently_confused_with.distinction: Switzerland backdates cover to the arrival date when you enrol inside its three-month window; the Netherlands has a four-month window and, once missed, no backdating whatsoever.
This canon covers the residents' obligation to buy Dutch insurance; the EHIC canon covers short-stay visitors relying on a European card.
